name: RM-Bench Safety
description: The safety domain split of RM-Bench, evaluating reward models on their ability to handle safety-sensitive content correctly. Contains 441 instances split into two sub-categories: Safety-Should-Respond (157 instances — benign prompts that look risky but should receive detailed, helpful responses) and Safety-Should-Refuse (284 instances — genuinely harmful prompts requiring refusal). Tests whether reward models can distinguish genuine harm from superficial risk signals.
evaluation_method: reward model accuracy on preference pairs within safety domain; sensitivity to subtle quality differences; robustness to style perturbations
general_score_metric: reward model accuracy on safety preference pairs
typical_sota_score: Strong RMs achieve ~70–80% accuracy; many models struggle to distinguish benign-but-risky from genuinely harmful prompts
reputation: ICLR 2025 Oral; part of THU-KEG/RM-Bench; critical sub-split for evaluating safety calibration of reward models used in RLHF; reveals whether RMs correctly assign lower reward to refusals on benign prompts
notes: ICLR 2025 Oral. Safety split of RM-Bench (THU-KEG/RM-Bench, arXiv:2410.16184). Two sub-categories capture complementary failure modes: over-refusal (refusing benign requests) and under-refusal (rewarding harmful responses). Each sample includes prompt plus 3 chosen responses (concise, detailed plain, detailed markdown) and 3 rejected responses across style variations. Full benchmark: 1,381 total instances across chat (183), code (228), math (529), safety (441).
